A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Em-Garde. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, computational-efficiency measurements, reward and threshold analyses, and qualitative demonstrations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and reports additional component ablations, training/testing threshold combinations, and a reward-coefficient experiment.

M1.justification: The IGPP proposer, SFT/GRPO training, LPMM embedding matcher, similarity-change triggering rule, and visual encoding cache remain unchanged. The component replacements introduced in v2 are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Parse2Prop-1K drawn from COIN, Ego4D, and BEHAVIOR, and evaluate the same StreamingBench, OVO-Bench, and ProactiveVideoQA tasks. The additional ablations introduce no new datasets, domains, or task scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds direct prompt-rewriting and yes/no decision replacements, their combined variant, and a naive sliding-window comparator. The comparison methods in the existing benchmark tables, including the appendix tables, are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled component-replacement experiments and explicitly crosses training and testing thresholds of 0.03, 0.035, and 0.04. It also adds lambda = 0.75 to the reward sweep. These extend the experimental settings; the primary setup, metrics, and default threshold remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands component validation by testing removal or replacement of IGPP, LPMM, and both together, plus a sliding-window control. It replaces the per-task threshold precision-recall analysis with a training/testing threshold grid and extends the reward sweep. The existing qualitative SFT-versus-RL analysis is retained in Appendix B.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Headline benchmark results remain unchanged. New diagnostic results include 24.0/28.8 without IGPP and 14.6/23.2 without LPMM in v2 Table 5, expressed as OVO-Bench F1/StreamingBench accuracy. Table 6 reports threshold-grid F1 values of 26.59-30.99, and Table 7 adds 28.6/36.4 at lambda = 0.75. The per-task precision-recall points in v1 Figure 5 are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, proposal and matching definitions, reward function, triggering rule, and recall/precision equations are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit priority claim that Em-Garde is the first proactive streaming framework to decompose triggering into query-time proposal generation and streaming-time matching. The abstract, conclusion, and principal accuracy and efficiency claims otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the component gains to the propose-match decomposition rather than model capacity, and explains threshold robustness through similarity changes and RL adaptation. It newly emphasizes stability across lambda values from 0.5 to 1, while removing the earlier task-specific threshold interpretation. The limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.5.1 newly specifies how the controls are constructed: Qwen2.5VL-7B for prompt rewriting, Qwen2VL-2B for yes/no decisions, and the query plus a two-second segment for the sliding-window baseline. Existing training hardware, training times, dataset-generation prompts, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The new explicit first-framework claim strengthens the paper's novelty positioning. The related-work discussion and cited-work membership otherwise remain unchanged; the bibliographies contain the same works.

P1.justification: Section 4.5 is locally rewritten and reordered, and its proposal-quality discussion moves into Appendix B.4. v2 also adds acknowledgements and author asterisks. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds component-ablation and threshold-grid tables, extends the reward table, and removes v1's precision-recall Figure 5. The proposal-quality Figure 4 moves to the appendix and is enlarged as Figure 7. Other tables and figures are largely retained with relocation, renumbering, and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The component controls and training/testing threshold grid strengthen evidence for the decomposition and its robustness. These are useful, limited gains, tempered by losing task-specific precision-recall diagnostics and a new prose mismatch: Section 4.5.1 says removing both modules performs worse, although Table 5 reports OVO-Bench F1 of 18.6 versus 14.6 when removing LPMM alone.
